uncited: This family computes the intersection of a ray with planar primitives, ranging from infinite planes to bounded rectangles and squares.
It solves the problem of determining entry and exit points for volume rendering traversal or hit testing for surface rendering.

It is distinguished from curved primitives (like [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md)) by relying on linear algebra and plane equations rather than quadratic surface definitions, and from general mesh intersection by operating on simple, analytically defined patches.
The analytical intersection of rays with planes is a foundational technique in computer graphics, dating back to the early days of ray tracing.
The infinite plane test is derived directly from the plane equation $\mathbf{N} \cdot (\mathbf{P} - \mathbf{P}_0) = 0$.
Bounded variants, such as axis-aligned rectangles and squares, add spatial constraints to this basic test.
